News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:18:58 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261127-us-thanksgiving-storms-cause-flooding-and-travel-chaos</link><description>
Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/97d15a54-ea55-11f1-9cd7-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261127-111335-111501-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/97d15a54-ea55-11f1-9cd7-81bc2b1dcd65/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261127-111335-111501-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9cbd74ee-ea55-11f1-8cc1-9bda5f9d0127</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 12:02:48 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261127-black-friday-the-evolution-of-a-shopping-phenomenon</link><description>
Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/796ad248-ea55-11f1-a00c-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261127-111142-111319-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/796ad248-ea55-11f1-a00c-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261127-111142-111319-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ea3a816-ea55-11f1-b196-89c658f0fd90</guid><pubDate>Fri, 27 Nov 2026 12:01:43 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261127-ukraine-residents-brace-for-another-difficult-winter</link><description>
As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck' ]]> Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star.

That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao.

A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER).

"The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events."

Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision

The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy, a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion.

Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years,

They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years.

Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits.

"A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. We took a closer look to discover a red giant, or a star that has started to expand toward the end of its life, just like our sun will one day," Karambelkar said. "Steady brightening was unusual, but even if something was stirring, no one expected to see an explosion in their lifetime, as these stars remain relatively stable for thousands of years."

An important clue to how this cataclysmic and cannibalistic event proceeded was provided by SPHEREx in July 2025, which found that before the eruption, Big Bao was fading in optical light but brightening in infrared. This indicated that Big Bao was cooling down and spewing out dense clouds of gas and dust that were enveloping the red giant star.

When Little Bao crashed into the core of Big Bao, it caused stellar material to be ejected at speeds of around 1.8 million miles per hour. This matter crashed into the envelope of gas and dust previously spewed by Big Bao, and this caused the flash of light seen on Oct. 17, 2025.

One of the final pieces of this story was provided by the JWST on Dec. 24, 2025. The powerful space telescope measured the total mass of dust and gas around Big Bao prior to the eruption since two months earlier.

This helped determine that Little Bao had a mass of around 70% of the sun's mass.

"It was kind of symbolic how the year was coming to an end as we managed to bring together the puzzle pieces from the story of Big and Little Bao," Karambelkar said. "But in my mind, this felt like a closure of just one chapter in a story that is just starting.

We learned so much about AT2025abao, but we also learned much about conducting coordinated, multi-facility, multi-team astronomical discoveries."

The team's research was published on Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.

On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars.

The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars, or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past.

It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface.

Why it mattered

It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet.

Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success.

After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars. It later found organic molecules on Mars as well.

Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health.

In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover, which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars.

And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise, is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon.

The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion.

What is it?

Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape.

This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud.

This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy, which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate.

The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy.

And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

   <link>https://www.denik.cz/historie/historie-obri-morsky-had-lod-niobe-zahada-1886/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=historie</link>
   <description>Před 140 lety, v sobotu 27. listopadu 1886, vyšel v příloze australských novin The Hamilton Spectator článek o podivném konci posádky velrybářské lodi Niobe, lovící v jižním Tichém oceánu. Loď potopil rozzuřený velrybí samec a na rybáře, kteří se stačili nalodit do záchranných člunů, začala během následujících nocí útočit tajemná nestvůra, popsaná přeživším členem posádky jako třiadvacetimetrový mořský had. Zvláštní přitom bylo, že podobná pozorování obřích mořských hadů se ten rok objevila na více místech. Šlo o sdílenou legendu? Nebo mohly mít tyto zprávy reálný základ?</description>

      <title>U Brna se objevila nebezpečná choroba vinné révy. Způsobit může značné škody</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/zlate-zloutnuti-choroba-vinna-reva-likvidace-vyskyt.A261127_142755_domaci_fohl#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ústřední kontrolní a zkušební ústav zemědělský (ÚKZÚZ) potvrdil výskyt agresivního kmene zlatého žloutnutí révy ve vinohradech u Hrušovan u Brna. Genotyp M54, který způsobuje v zahraničí vážné hospodářské škody, dosud v Česku odborníci nezjistili. Nyní jej odhalili na 29 testovaných keřích.</description>

      <title>Dělal jí nechutné oplzlosti a tvrdil, že léčí. Seniora odsoudili za zneužívání školačky</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/plzen/zpravy/soud-maser-zneuzivani-divky-plzen-klatovsko.A260519_123041_vary-zpravy_vb#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>I když měl živnost na masérské služby, za sedmdesátiletým Josefem H. do Lešišova na Klatovsku jezdili lidé z okolí jako k vyhlášenému léčiteli. Akce začíná v 16 hodin v sobotu 12. prosince 2026 v Tibetském domě na Asijské poznávací stezce.
